title: An Explainable Multi-Criteria Pipeline for Automated miRNA Interaction Extraction from Biomedical Literature
content: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are short non-coding RNAs that regulate post-transcriptional gene expression, and their dysregulation is associated with numerous pathologies, including cancers. However, evidence of miRNA-gene and miRNA-pathology interactions remains scattered across more than 100,000 articles indexed on PubMed, making manual curation impractical on a large scale. We present an automated biomedical text mining pipeline that collects PubMed literature, extracts mentions of miRNAs, genes, and pathologies using a hybrid approach combining regular expressions and BioBERT semantic similarity, and then identifies and prioritizes candidate interactions using an explainable multi-criteria plausibility score. On a validation corpus of 728 articles processed in 9 runs, the system extracted 7,884 segmented sentences, identified 2,097 distinct biomedical entities, and generated 87 accepted candidate relationships versus 20 rejected ones with a traced pattern—illustrating the pipeline's ability to operate at scale while maintaining a complete audit trail for each filtering decision.Unlike confidence scores derived from end-to-end neural models, each acceptance or rejection decision remains auditable: six conjunctive rules, each associated with an interpretable rejection code, guarantee the traceability of each filtered candidate.The system is based on a layered architecture reusing LangGraph for orchestration, incremental SQLite persistence for reproducibility, and a web dashboard for human oversight. A cascade classification (lexical rules, similarity-based matching, fallback to a local LLM) ensures high coverage while maintaining entirely local operation. Quantitative precision/recall validation on a manually annotated subcorpus established a baseline precision of 16.0% (recall 80.0%); five additional entity-agnostic classification rules, each individually validated against ground truth before deployment, raised precision to 37.5% while recall reached and remained at 100%.
